newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases back to 9.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases back to 9.0 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate eased back to 9.0 percent on Monday from 10.7 percent despite a higher demand for kuna funds on the local money market.
Dealers said supply, totalling 48.9 million kuna, fell short of demand for longer-term bank borrowings. These were made at up to 15 percent a year last Friday.
Interbank rates were unchanged at 9-11 percent. Insurers raised to 9.0 from 8.0 percent their rate on previous loans.
The week-end overnight trade totalled a meagre 13.8 million kuna, of which some 50 percent were borrowings for statutory reserve payment.
The central bank's kuna midrate for Tuesday eased to 5.4458 against the dollar and to 3.5598 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
